AutoRek Supports Leading UK Digital Investment Platforms as Demand for Automated Reconciliation Grows
summary:
AutoRek, the leader in enterprise financial controls and reconciliation automation, today announced that two leading digital investment platforms in the UK have selected its technology to automate reconciliation processes, strengthen financial controls and support operational resilience at scale.
Together, the platforms serve more than 3.3 million customers and oversee more than £140 billion in client and platform assets, highlighting the growing operational demands facing digital investment providers as investor participation and transaction volumes continue to increase.
As digital investment platforms scale, firms are under increasing pressure to manage complex data flows and high transaction volumes while maintaining accurate records, robust controls and efficient operations. Manual reconciliation processes can create operational bottlenecks and make it more difficult for firms to scale without adding significant resources.
AutoRek enables financial services organisations to automate reconciliation, exception management and financial controls, using AutoRek ARIA, its intelligence engine for financial control, to help teams identify likely matches, understand anomalies and prioritise investigation. This reduces manual effort while keeping human judgement, review and approval at the centre of the reconciliation lifecycle. 
“Digital investment platforms are operating at a scale where manual processes can quickly become a constraint on growth, while the need for robust financial controls only increases as volumes rise,” said Martyn Ward, CRO at AutoRek. “These customer wins demonstrate the growing demand for reconciliation technology that can handle scale while giving firms greater control, transparency and operational resilience. By automating processes that have traditionally relied heavily on manual intervention, firms can build a stronger operational foundation as their businesses continue to grow.”
The two customer wins reflect a broader shift across the UK digital investment sector, where platforms are increasingly focused on improving the scalability and resilience of their operating models. AutoRek's technology provides automated matching, break management and configurable financial controls designed to support organisations as transaction volumes and operational complexity increase.
The new relationships build on AutoRek's growing presence across the financial services sector, where it works with organisations to automate critical reconciliation and financial control processes.

August Breaks UK Credit Card Record as Balances Soar
summary:
According to data analysis from global analytics software leader FICO, average active UK credit card balances exceeded £2,000 in August for the first time since records began, following three consecutive months of increases. Contributing to higher balances, payment rates dropped after a brief recovery in July, and remain lower than the same time last year. This trend, coupled with an annual increase in all levels of missed payments, highlights the importance of risk teams continuing to closely monitor for signs of financial difficulty.
Highlights
Average spending increased by 3.1% month-on-month to £840, growing 3.3% year-on-year and marking the highest annual growth rate in over a year.
The average active balance grew 1.2% month-on-month to a record £2,005 and remains up 4.8% year-on-year.
The percentage of overall balance paid fell 1.1% on the previous month, to 33.3%, and is down 3.1% year-on-year.
Average credit limits crossed £6,000 for the first time, and overlimit accounts grew 4.7% month-on-month to an average overlimit of £95. This is down -3.1% on the previous month but up 3.3% year-on-year.
The percentage of customers missing one payment fell by 7.1% month-on-month but balances for these accounts rose 5.1% year-on-year, to £2,520.
Accounts with two missed payments climbed 2.8% compared to July, but are 9.5% higher year-on-year. Annual growth for balances of these accounts slowed to 1.8%, with the average standing at £2,945.
There was a slight monthly decline of 0.7% in three missed payments, but year-on-year there was a sharp increase of 16.4%. Average balances grew 1.7% on the year, reaching £3,320.
FICO Comment:
August marked significant milestones, as average active balances passed £2,000 and credit limits exceeded £6,000 for the first time. The year-on-year shortfall in payment rates narrowed for a third consecutive month, while overlimit accounts showed year-on-year improvement. This suggests that acute affordability pressures from earlier in the year are beginning to ease slightly, despite the persistent pressure on finances that has characterised the market since early 2025. However, late payments across all three cycles remain higher than in 2025, reflecting a macroeconomic environment that continues to stretch household budgets.
UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August, up from 2.9% in July, driven in part by rising food prices. With Ofgem’s energy price cap set to increase, borrowing costs are unlikely to fall significantly before winter. Meanwhile, total UK credit card debt has reached a record £82.4 billion according to the Bank of England, alongside record-high representative credit card interest rates.
Given these cost pressures, risk teams should monitor whether the recent stability in payment rates and overlimit accounts can be sustained. Although one-cycle delinquency fell sharply in August, it remains 5.1% higher year-on-year. As the primary entry point to the delinquency pipeline, and with CPI and energy costs both rising into autumn, early intervention and tailored support for this population should be prioritised before further seasonal pressure builds
NoYesCredit Cards20 Oct, 2026
content: UK credit card balances exceeded £2,000 for the first time in August, according to FICO data, driven by rising spending and falling payment rates. Average credit limits also crossed £6,000. While some affordability pressures eased slightly, missed payments remained higher year-on-year amid ongoing economic challenges, including rising inflation and energy costs.
